newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open little moved, Budget awaited.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open little moved, Budget awaited.

text.p: Singapore shares barely moved in early trading on Friday. Dealers said they expected stocks to stay in a tight range ahead of the announcement of the Budget from 0800 GMT.
"My feeling is that Singapore will trade a bit lower in thin volumes ahead of the Budget," said a dealer at a Japanese broking house.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index eased 4.09 points to 1,964.25 at 0201 GMT.
"Bank stocks are up just a little bit or unchanged and there hasn't been much bargain hunting or short covering after yesterday's fall," he said.
Dealers said foreign funds were disenchanted with the region as a whole in light of volatility in currency movements.
"Singapore is the eye of the storm. People just want to get out of the region," said the dealer from the Japanese firm.
Another dealer said some of Singapore's weakness was in sympathy with Malaysia's stock fallout after Bank Negara said it would defend the ringgit under speculative attack.
The Philippines this morning said it would allow the peso to move in a wider range against the dollar.
"There should still be some confidence in Singapore and Malaysia's currencies," one dealer said.
One dealer said blue chips could claw their way up a bit near the close. "The Budget may be a non-event," he said.
Others said the market would fall if there were no tax incentives for businesses, at least for the manufacturing sector.

Creative Technology headed the gainers up Singapore $0.70 to S$27.40 on light volumes. Singapore Telecom ticked up S$0.01 to S$2.57 on 1.5 million units, including crossed trades totalling 830,000 shares at various prices.
